chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ays ibn al-Qasim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has cattle, can he sell their milk without measuring? He said: Yes, until it stops or something from it.

key_terms.يَنْقَطِعَ: It stops (referring to the flow of milk from the udder)

ai.seo_question: Can a person sell milk from their cattle without measuring it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) permits the sale of milk from livestock without precise weighing or measuring, provided the milk is fresh and distinct from the udder. This ruling highlights the flexibility in commercial transactions (*mu'amalat*) regarding perishable goods, distinguishing between the uncertainty of quantity (*gharar*) and the certainty of the commodity's existence and quality. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that minor uncertainties in measurement are tolerated for items like milk, which are consumed quickly and are naturally variable.
